7:
One need not check proactively (min ha-stam, without cause to assume there would be an injury) any part of the animal for Treifot (specific terminal injuries) except the lungs of domesticated and wild species of mammals to see if there is a Sirkha (strands of connective tissue) (ריב"ש ור"י ן' חביב וע"פ). Anyone who "breaches the fence" to eat meat without checking the lungs should be bitten by a snake.

Rema: We have the custom to also inflate every lung, even if there is nothing wrong with it (ש"ד סימן צ"ב ובדיקות וע"פ). In some places they are lenient and don't inflate the lungs unless there was a Sircha removed by rubbing, and this is the main understanding (רמב"ם פי"א מרדכי וע"פ)

If one opened the abdomen of the animal and, before the lungs were inspected, a dog or an idol worshipper came and took them, it is permitted to eat this animal and we are not concerned that they may have been punctured or had sirchot.

Rema: There are those who are strict in the case that the lungs were lost (בה"ג וראב"ן ור"י הלוי ומרדכי והג"א וע"פ) and the animal should not be permitted in such a case except if it will be a major financial loss or if the animal were a kid, lamb, or a wild species, as sirkhot are uncommon amongst them (טור בשם בעה"ת).
If an idol worshipper or a Jew came and removed the lungs before they were checked and they are still available, one inflates them.

If one is uncertain as to whether (the sircha) is on the back of the lobe or in the chituch and when the lungs are inflated a lot it appears that (the sircha) is in the chituch but when the lungs are not fully inflated the sircha appears to be outside (the chituch) the animal is kosher.

A sirkha connected from the varda lobe to anywhere is treifah, even to its own pouch and even if the whole lobe is connected to it. This is the law for any extra piece of lung, that any sirkha makes it a treifah.

Rema: However, if the varda is connected below from its source (point of attachment) to its pouch it is possible to say it is kosher, since this is the majority (of the varda) (בית יוסף בשם מהר"י ן' חביב).

If an Ona (lobe) or Oma (caudal lobe) becomes Nirsakh to the Gargaret (windpipe), Chazzeh (chest), heart fat or its envelope (kisso), or the Tarfash (a ‎rag-like, ‎irregularly ‎shaped ‎organ, ‎membrane etc.) (pericardium) of the heart, or Tarfash of the liver, or the Tarfash of the Iynunita (? see 35:2) which is the end of the Tarfash of the heart, or to the womb or the elmera which is called molyega or a bronchus that runs between the two weaves (rows?) (R"Y N' Chaviv and D"A) or the Kaneh (aorta?) of the heart or the fat of the bronchia or the liver - it's treif, even if it's stuck to one of these places without Pilush (going through) (Ibid. and other Achronim AB"Y).

Rema: And some are lenient if the upper lobes that are close to the Gargaret are actually stuck to the Gargaret with no division between them at all where one can insert his finger between them (מרדכי פא"ט בשם ראבי"ה ובה"ג ומהרי"ו ואגודה). Likewise if the Onot or Omot were completely stuck from top to bottom to the fat that descends between the lungs (Ibid., R"B and R"Ch). Likewise if the whole lung was stuck to the spine, for we say that's the way it grows so it's not a Sirkha (MHRY"V). And all this should not be permitted without asking someone who's a Chakham and expert halakhic decisor, and one may not learn from these places to other places where the lung is Nirsakh, for the other places have no distinction whether all of it is stuck or not (D"A and MB"Y).

Sirkha Teluya, a sirkha emerging from the lung that hangs without being stuck to any place, is kosher and needs no checking.

Rema: A Sirkha emerging from a Boah (cyst) is treif (B"Y in the name of Raabad, Rokeach, and MHRY"V); but from a Tinri it's kosher (MHRY"V and see above, 37:2).

A Sirkha from a place to place [i.e. the same part?] such as a lobe or on the caudal lobe itself, has the same rule as a Sirkha Teluya.

Rema: And specifically when the Sirkha is shorter than the flesh of the lung when the lung is inflated, but if it's so short that the strength of the Sirkha causes the flesh under it to be restrained and not rise like the rest of the lung when inflated it's treif (M"hra of Prague and Bedikot latter version) And a Sirkha Teluya that also rises when the lung is inflated or has a wound on the wall facing it is treif (Bedikot old version).

Whenever a lung Srukha is forbidden, it makes no difference if the Sirkha is thin as a strand of hair or if it's thick, strong and wide as a thumb; it's not like those that (crush, rub) it by hand and if it breaks they think one can be lenient; and whoever practices that is as if he feeds treifot to Yisrael.

There's someone that wrote that he inserts his finger under the Sirkha and lifts it a little; if it breaks due to any amount of lifting it's a Sirkha Bat Yoma (within one day old) and kosher. But one should not be lenient like this, except with a beast of an Yisrael, and this leniency should not be relied on except with a bodek who's more religiously fit and H' fearing than most.
It's good to water the beast close to Shekhita.

There's an opinion that says that the Bodek inserts his hand in the beast quickly and without a relaxed hand, and if any Sikhra breaks apart when the Bodek inserts his hand, he brings the lung out and checks it. If it has Sirkha he locates its start in the lung or on the wall, otherwise it's Rir (mucus, spittle) and it's kosher. And one may not use this leniency except with a beast of Yisrael, and one may not rely on this leniency except with a bodek who is kosher and exceptionally H' fearing.

Rema: And there are those that permit feeling the Sirkhot and crushing them, and they say a Sirkha, if a person crushes it all day it won't sever, and therefore wherever it gets crushed they hold one should be lenient, and they say it's not a Sirkha but just Rir (spittle) (MHRY"V and Kol Bo). And even though it's very much a leniency, it's already the practice of all the people in these lands, and they should not be reprimanded, since they have what to rely on. But nevertheless the Bodek needs to be God fearing, that he knows to be careful to crush gently so it's not severed by force. And there are places where they don't practice crushing and feeling the Sirkhot of the Varda if it's Nirsakh to another place, and any place that's Nirsakh makes it treif (so I heard and so it seems from the language of R' D. ibn Chiyya shbb'y). And there are places where their practice is being lenient even in this, but to me it seems the first opinion (is right), to not crush in the Varda, and any Sirkhot that are not in their order, since the Sirkha that's not in their order is treif is mentioned in the Gemara, so there's no arguing with that; there's no relying on those that say to be lenient regarding crushing and feeling (and so it sounds from the language of MHRY"V, no arguing). But the practice in our city is to feel and crush all the Sirkhot and there's no difference between one Sirkha and another, but it's proper to mind what I wrote if it's not a great loss. Also the practice in our city is to regard treif any Sirkha of lambs and tela'im (sic), and young cows, and not crush them at all, for there's a kabbalah in this, to reckon them treif, for the Sirkha is still soft and will get severed by crushing.
A Bodek who removes his hand and said it's treif and then another one inserts his hand and says he's found no treifot - the first one is believed.

If the Tabach (slaughterer) that inserted his hand said it's treif and then it's clarified that the Tarfash had not been opened, so it's found that the Tabach had not touched the lung, and they opened the Tarfash and checked it and find no treifot, we rule it kosher.

If the Bodek said they're not in order and later someone contradicts him and says they're in order the beast retains its presumptive status of permissibility [that it gets after being shekhted, Chullin 9a].

If someone buys a lung and says he found Sirkha in it in a place that makes it treif, but the seller says it was in a place where it's kosher - when the two of them come at one time to the Beit Din there's no Edut, testimony, so behold it's like a beast that had its lung get lost before checking.

Rema: Likewise in places where they shekht among idolaters and they left the beast with the idolaters between shekhting and checking - we don't worry that the idolater inserted his hand and broke the Sirkhot, since checking the lungs is d'Rabbanan so Sfeika Lehakel (Rashba #298). However if the idolater slaughterers are accustomed to do so then there's reason do worry even Bediavad; and Lekhatchila one should be careful in this whole matter.

A lung that's punctured at a sectioning of the lobes on the back of the lobe facing the (chest) wall and the wall seals it with a Sirkha on the flesh that's between the ribs or between flesh and bone - it's kosher. But if it's a Sirkha to bone alone it's treif. This is also the rule with anything that's intact facing the lobes on top, even if it's tangled [with the flesh of the wall, Chullin 48b] - it's kosher, since the space is narrow and pressed against the wall and it seals it. And it's called Dofen (wall) until the Chut (line?) where they M'naker (do Nikkur, removing the forbidden fats) from the chest, and from there onwards it's called Chazzeh (chest), and if it's Nirsakh there it's treif, and if it's Nirsakh on the Chut that's in the Chazzeh its rule is as if it's Nirsakh in the Chazzeh and it's treif.

Rema: But for us there's no consequence in these distinctions, and also in all the parts till the end of this Siman. Because it's already the custom in these lands to consider them all treif, and one may not deviate, for it's a custom of the forefathers in Germano-Franco lands, of whom we're descendants, therefore no Sirkha in the lung may be considered kosher except two lobes Serukhot in their order below, at their root, and it's the same rule for an Ona to an Oma at a place where they're in their order; only such cases; and we've already explained that they were lenient with a Sirkha that breaks by squeezing it.
And specifically facing the Onot is when it can be ruled kosher, but if it's not facing the Onot is treif.

It's ruled kosher specifically when the hole is facing the wall, but if it's pierced from inside, even if it's in the lower parts of the lung, and a Sirkha comes out from there to the wall it's treif. And if a Sirkha goes out from the lower parts of the lobe and spreads on the back of the Ona and is Nirsakh to the wall, if the majority of the Sirkha is on the back of the Ona it's kosher and if not it's treif.

It the Sirkha rises from the Ona to the wall that's on the side of the Oma it's treif, and if the Sirkha rises from the Ona to [both] the wall facing the Ona and to the wall facing the Oma we go according to the majority.

If the Oma is Serukha to the wall, if there's a wound on the wall it's kosher and it needs no Bedika and if there's no wound on the wall it's treif and Bedika is ineffective, and specifically in the case of a Serukha to the wall we rule it kosher by a wound but if Serukha to other places such as the chest, throat, heart fat or pouch and so forth even though they have a wound it's treif and Bedika is not effective.

This wound they're talking about is when the wall has something that looks like Nega, plague. But if there's only shiny black spots (beharot shechorot) it's not a real sign of a wound. And if a rib was broken even though it mended back together we say it's fine, [it's a] wound.

If the whole lung is attached to the wall, if there's no wound on the wall it's treif, and Bedika is ineffective for it even if all of it is attached with no separation. And there's an opinion written that if someone permits it he's bar nidui, censured, and his vessels are prohibited (Rashbatz).

If the Oma and Ona are nirsakh with one sirkha to the wall, if most of the sirkha is from the Ona it's kosher and if most from the Oma it's treif, if there's no wound on the wall. And so too if if the Ona is serukha with one sirkha to the chest and the wall we go according to the majority, and so too if the Oma is serukha by one sirkha to the wall that has a wound and the sirkha is on the wound and outwards from it, if the majority is on the wound it's kosher and if not it's treif. And so too in the Oma is nirsakh by one sirkha to the envelope and to the wound that's on the wall - if the majority is on the wound on the wall it's kosher and if not it's treif.

Rema: A lung on which is found something like a chelev covering and it's fleshy without peeling this [covering] off it - if the lung underlying it is intact and looks good it's kosher, however the lung needs Bedika by inflation (B"Y 66:38 in the name of Rokeach).
